issue: Can a federal prisoner use a § 2241 petition under the § 2255(e) savings clause to challenge a mandatory career-offender enhancement as 'actual innocence,' where a later retroactive Supreme Court decision shows a prior conviction is not a predicate offense?

sides.position: A career-offender misclassification based on a later retroactive Supreme Court decision can support a § 2241 actual-innocence claim under the § 2255(e) savings clause, at least for pre-Booker mandatory sentences.
A claim that a prior conviction was wrongly treated as a predicate offense is a legal-insufficiency argument, not factual innocence, so it cannot proceed as actual innocence under the savings clause.
cases: Damon v. United States, 732 F.3d 1 (1st Cir. 2013)
Okereke v. United States, 307 F.3d 117 (3d Cir. 2002)
Sandlain v. English, 714 F. App'x 827 (10th Cir. 2017)
McCarthan v. Director of Goodwill Industries-Suncoast, Inc., 851 F.3d 1076 (11th Cir. 2017) (en banc)

this_court: Allen v. Ives holds that the claim is cognizable as actual innocence under § 2241 and that the circuit is aligned with the Fourth, Sixth, and Seventh Circuits.
quote: We agree with our dissenting colleague's argument that there is a circuit split.
cite: Michael Allen v. Richard Ives, 976 F.3d 863 (9th Cir. 2020)
